result.summary: Our patch closes the primary CVE vector — reflected XSS via the JSONP `callback` parameter — using the standard JSONP defense: an allowlist regex that requires the callback to be a (dotted) JavaScript identifier, enforced before the value is ever written. It is applied at every callback write path: `AgentServlet.sendAllJSON`, `JolokiaHttpHandler.sendAllJSON`, and the shared `IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose` sink (covering both servlet and jvm streaming). POV no longer reproduces and regressions pass. The one gap versus the official fix is that the official also sanitizes the response mime type (`MimeTypeUtil.sanitize` / `getResponseMimeType`), a secondary CWE-079 hardening our patch omits.
result.root_cause: Attacker-controlled `callback` request parameter is concatenated verbatim into the response body as `callback + "(" + json + ");"` (and streamed equivalently), allowing arbitrary markup to be reflected; the sink must reject any callback that isn't a bare JavaScript identifier.

dimensions.rationale: Callback markup-injection class is fully blocked at all sink paths by an anchored identifier allowlist; POV no longer reproduces. Loses a point because the mime-type reflection path (Content-Type via mimeType param) that the official fix closes remains open.
dimensions.evidence: IoUtil.validateCallback + CALLBACK_PATTERN; calls in AgentServlet.sendAllJSON, JolokiaHttpHandler.sendAllJSON, IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose; getMimeType still returns raw request mimeType
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Neutralizes the flaw at the write boundary via allowlist before any output, including the shared IoUtil sink, matching the official intent; slightly less central than the official early-handle() check.
dimensions.evidence: validateCallback invoked as first statement in streamResponseAndClose and before content assembly in both sendAllJSON methods
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

dimensions.rationale: All four callback write paths (servlet+jvm × buffered+streaming) are covered via the shared sink and per-site checks; the mimeType reflection variant addressed by official MimeTypeUtil.sanitize is not covered.
dimensions.evidence: IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose validation covers both streaming callers; AgentServlet/JolokiaHttpHandler sendAllJSON guarded; no change to getMimeType
dimensions.label: Completeness / variants

dimensions.rationale: Same defensive strategy as official (validate callback is a valid JS function name via regex); different location (at sink vs validateCallbackIfGiven in handle/doHandle) and allows dotted names, which is a superset the upstream project later adopted.
dimensions.label: Developer-intent alignment

dimensions.rationale: Regressions pass, legitimate simple and dotted (angular.callbacks._0) callbacks preserved; throwing IllegalArgumentException at the sink is less graceful than the official early check but breaks no valid input.
dimensions.evidence: regressions_passed=true; checkDottedCallbackAllowed test; validation precedes any write so no partial output
dimensions.label: Functional correctness

dimensions.rationale: Regex is fully anchored and linear (no ReDoS); does not echo the offending value (no reflected error). Minor: an unhandled IllegalArgumentException thrown deep in sendAllJSON may surface as a 500/stacktrace rather than a clean JSON error.
dimensions.evidence: Pattern.compile linear alternation; throw new IllegalArgumentException without echoing pCallback
dimensions.label: No new defects

dimensions.rationale: Tight, well-placed change: one shared validation helper plus three call sites at the exact sinks, with focused tests.
dimensions.label: Minimality

dimensions.rationale: For JSONP, allowlisting the callback to a valid JS identifier is the defense-of-record (output encoding is not applicable to a function name); implemented with a correct anchored allowlist, matching the official approach.
dimensions.evidence: CALLBACK_PATTERN identifier allowlist mirroring official MimeTypeUtil.isValidCallback
dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: The response mime type is not sanitized. The official fix routes Content-Type through MimeTypeUtil.getResponseMimeType/sanitize (allowlisting application/json or text/plain), but our patch leaves getMimeType returning the raw attacker-supplied mimeType parameter, leaving a secondary CWE-079 / content-type-confusion vector open.

Validation throws IllegalArgumentException at the sink (inside sendAllJSON / streamResponseAndClose) rather than early in handle()/doHandle(); this can surface as an ungraceful 500/stack trace instead of the official clean JSON error response, though no malicious content is written.
